problem: Scene-graph representations (ConceptGraphs, VLMaps, HOV-SG) give semantic memory but downstream navigation still needs dense metric maps or global metric localization; other VLN systems rely on step-by-step language decisions or online exploration without prior map knowledge.
motivation: Long-range navigation with sequential decisions or online exploration accumulates errors and wastes steps. A single lightweight graph that supports open-vocabulary grounding, relocalization and execution would remove the need for dense metric reconstruction.
key_idea: Build an object-path graph (a hierarchical open-vocabulary object/room scene graph plus a traversability node graph with panoramic semantic snapshots) and navigate it via Dijkstra global planning plus object-keypoint angular visual servoing between nodes.
insight: Hierarchical structure (room, supporter, relations) improves instance grounding; the ablation shows removing supporters hurts most (NSR 0.77 / SPL 0.32 vs full 0.88 / 0.42). Similarity-weighted keypoint servoing helps (NSR 0.82 to 0.88 with weighting). More stored objects per node and panoramic views reduce translation error, and narrow 90° FOV with fewer than 8 keypoints causes off-route navigation.
method: Open-vocabulary 3D object mapping: SAM masks are back-projected with depth and odometry, merged by geometric overlap and CLIP cosine similarity, features fused with point-count weights, and captions refined by VLM+LLM.

Object scene graph: rooms are segmented with EDF and labeled by an LLM; objects are split into supporters and regular objects by 3D bbox volume, linked to rooms/supporters, with LLM-predicted semantic edges between adjacent objects and doorway links between rooms.

Traversability graph: nodes are added along the trajectory when view similarity (shared visible objects) drops, plus doorway nodes and sampled free-space nodes; edges are collision-free straight lines, with extra nodes to connect disconnected components.
Node initialization: a rotation-invariant semantic panoramic descriptor (N angular bins) from a short exploration is matched by cosine similarity to node descriptors to find the start node.
Global topological planning: the query is grounded hierarchically (room, supporter, object) via an LLM-parsed query, and Dijkstra gives a node path to the target node.

Semantic visual servoing: object keypoints (centroid, label, feature) in the current view are matched to the next node's panoramic snapshot; the controller uses relative angular residuals between consecutive keypoints, similarity-weighted, mapped to (vx,vy) then unicycle (v, ω), stopping when ||e||<ε.

setting.backbone: SAM + CLIP + VLM captioner + LLM (frozen, off-the-shelf); no learned navigation policy
setting.observation: RGB-D with odometry/pose; panoramic snapshots at nodes
setting.action_space: continuous linear velocity (vx,vy) mapped to unicycle (v, ω)
setting.simulator: HM3D and Replica (Habitat-based scenes), plus real world
setting.privileged: Map is built beforehand from recorded trajectory with poses (pre-exploration); the target object must be correctly grounded as goal node; odometry is used for mapping

numbers.extra: pre-built map; goal node from retrieved object
numbers.evidence: Table 'Object navigation performance in terms of SPL from 10 different start points.' Avg. SPL 0.408

numbers_note: Not on standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks; small custom evaluations (4 scenes). Ablation full model reports NSR 0.88 / SPL 0.42, inconsistent with the 0.91 NSR average. Translation-error results only in a figure.
results: The object-path graph reaches an average query SR of 0.83 versus 0.74 for HOV-SG, 0.68 for VLMaps and 0.60 for ConceptGraphs. Average SPL is 0.408 versus 0.37 for HOV-SG. Node relocalization is comparable to SceneGraphLoc, and inter-node navigation achieves NSR 0.91 and PLR 1.23.
limitations: Node-by-node servoing stops at relay nodes and does not optimize global path smoothness (PLR 1.23).
Evaluation is small and custom (4 scenes, 120 queries), with no standard VLN benchmarks, and real-world validation is only a qualitative single-transition example.
Assumes a pre-built map and static environments; dynamic environments are left to future work.
